source.title: Tko si ti kad nitko ne gleda? O identitetu, maskama i susretu sa sobom

summary.title_hr: Tko si ti kad nitko ne gleda? O identitetu, maskama i susretu sa sobom
summary.abstract_hr: Ova epizoda podcasta istražuje duboko pitanje identiteta žena, posebno kada se suočavaju sa sobom bez društvenih uloga i očekivanja. Razgovor se dotiče tereta koje žene nose, potrebe za tišinom i autentičnošću, te važnosti podrške i ranjivosti. Epizoda naglašava kako se žene mogu osjećati preplavljeno i izgubljeno, te kako pronalaženje sebe i prihvaćanje vlastite ranjivosti, uz duhovnu perspektivu, može dovesti do istinskog oslobođenja. Također, najavljuje se konferencija koja će ženama pružiti prostor za dublji susret sa sobom.
key_points: Žene su često više uključene u duhovne inicijative i rad na sebi, ali nose terete očekivanja i ideala, što dovodi do osjećaja rasula i nemogućnosti da se o tome govori.
Potrebno je dopuštenje da je 'ok' biti loš, umoran ili u procesu, umjesto davanja savjeta i osjećaja krivnje, jer Isus ne donosi takve stvari.
Tišina je ključna potreba za žene, ali je teško pronaći u današnjem užurbanom životu, što dovodi do preopterećenosti živčanog sustava i nemogućnosti opuštanja.
Definiranje problema, poput anksioznosti umjesto nedostatka vjere, donosi olakšanje i oslobođenje, jer je zbunjujuće ne znati s čime se borimo.
Očekivanja od žena su se promijenila; danas se od njih očekuje da rade izvan kuće, ali i da održavaju dom, što stvara veći teret u usporedbi s prošlim generacijama.
Pružanje podrške i viđenosti, bez davanja savjeta, donosi veliko olakšanje i prihvaćanje, jer mnogi nikada nisu osjetili da ih je netko saslušao.
Maske se nose zbog straha od ranjivosti, povrijeđenosti ili neprihvaćanja, a istinsko prihvaćanje dolazi tek kada se pokaže autentično ja, čak i ako to znači suočavanje s kritikom.
Konferencija 'Tko sam ja kad nitko ne gleda?' nudi prostor za žene da skinu maske, pronađu tišinu i dožive dublji susret sa sobom uz Božju perspektivu, s ciljem konkretne promjene i uvida.
summary.title_en: Who are you when no one is watching? On identity, masks and the encounter with oneself
summary.abstract_en: This podcast episode explores the deep question of women's identity, especially when they face themselves without social roles and expectations. The conversation touches upon the burdens that women carry, the need for silence and authenticity, and the importance of support and vulnerability. The episode emphasizes how women can feel overwhelmed and lost, and how finding oneself and accepting one's own vulnerability, along with a spiritual perspective, can lead to true liberation. Also, a conference is announced that will provide women with a space for a deeper encounter with themselves.
key_points_en: Women are often more involved in spiritual initiatives and work on themselves, but they carry the burdens of expectations and ideals, which leads to a feeling of disarray and the inability to speak about it.
Permission is needed that it is 'ok' to be bad, tired, or in a process, instead of giving advice and a feeling of guilt, because Jesus does not bring such things.
Silence is a key need for women, but it is difficult to find in today's busy life, which leads to overload of the nervous system and the inability to relax.
Defining the problem, such as anxiety instead of a lack of faith, brings relief and liberation, because it is confusing not to know what we are fighting against.
Expectations of women have changed; today it is expected of them to work outside the house, but also to maintain the home, which creates a greater burden in comparison with past generations.
Providing support and visibility, without giving advice, brings great relief and acceptance, because many have never felt that someone listened to them.
Masks are worn because of the fear of vulnerability, hurt, or non-acceptance, and true acceptance comes only when the authentic self is shown, even if that means facing criticism.

The conference 'Who am I when no one is watching?' offers space for women to take off masks, find silence, and experience a deeper encounter with themselves with God's perspective, with the goal of concrete change and insight.
